method: The two dirty limits come from vm.dirty_background_ratio, the percentage of available memory at which the kernel's background flusher threads start writeback, and vm.dirty_ratio, the percentage at which a process generating disk writes starts writing pages out itself and blocks until the dirty set drains. The kernel measures both against free plus reclaimable pages, which is not total RAM; the page multiplies the RAM entered by each ratio and rounds half up to a whole MiB, so every threshold reads as an upper bound and moves with the RAM figure rather than with the memory free at that instant. A background ratio at or above the hard ratio is refused, because the hard limit would be reached first and the background threshold would never fire. The headroom is the hard threshold minus the background threshold. The flusher wakes every vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs hundredths of a second, so a steady write rate deposits that rate times the wake interval per wake, and vm.dirty_expire_centisecs sets the age at which dirty pages are written out on the next wake. Dividing the background threshold by the write rate gives the age of the oldest dirty data when that threshold is reached, which the page compares with the expiry so a steady stream that ages pages out before reaching the threshold says so. Dirty data only accumulates when the sustained write rate exceeds the device's write throughput: the excess is the growth rate, and the time to each threshold is that threshold divided by the excess, so a workload the device can retire never reaches either limit and both time fields are null. Rates accept decimals, a decimal comma, exponent notation, a unicode minus and surrounding spaces; RAM is whole MiB from 128 to 16,777,216, the ratios whole percent, and the two intervals whole centisecs, and blank, non-numeric or out-of-range values are refused rather than clamped. The model assumes a constant dirty rate, a constant device throughput and no other writers, and it does not model writeback congestion, cgroup v2 dirty limits, zswap, per-bdi limits or the kernel's own page accounting, so the times are a planning bound rather than a measurement. Nothing is probed, stored or sent.
